title: Firewall linkage
summary: A peerage is the only thing that puts an address into the fence. The static nftables file keeps the skeleton (default drop, loopback, established, DHCP, an empty set xtp_peers admitting IP protocol 36). xtpd adds a peer's address when the peerage is taken and removes it when the peerage is withdrawn or its fence lapses, through the firewall controller's narrow nft helper, which touches named sets only and refuses protected sources. At start xtpd empties the set and rebuilds it; at stop it withdraws.
authority: design (architecture Tom Dyer; written by Claude (Opus 5.5), 2026-11-24)
invariants: No application, hook or MI writes a firewall rule
Clean at both ends: start rebuilds, stop withdraws
procedure: Mutate only the named set xtp_peers through libexec/firewall-nft

provenance.claim: Narrow nft mutation helper; protected-source registry

qualification_boundaries.status: dev1 built: packages/oorexx_xtpd_v0.1-dev1 (Claude (Opus 5.5), 24 Nov 2026) - registrations, peerages and keys from files, unix-socket OPEN with descriptor passing, exec hooks, the fence, receipts through oorexx_logging
qualification_boundaries.field: tested on loopback only (two daemons, real OpenSSH over UDP and raw IP 36); not field-tested; LDAP inputs, operating states, emergency files and the role bootstrap are not built
